question: Should OpenClaw adopt OPENCLAW_LOCALE as a durable process-wide operator-locale contract for the CLI and future localization surfaces, and if so what precedence and documentation guarantees must it provide?
rationale: This is new public environment behavior spanning a dependency-ordered localization series; source review cannot determine the desired long-term configuration and compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve a documented process-locale contract
options.body: Define precedence, supported surfaces, fallback behavior, and upgrade expectations for OPENCLAW_LOCALE before the series uses it broadly.

options.title: Keep locale selection surface-local
options.body: Limit this PR to existing onboarding or UI locale preferences and avoid introducing a new process-wide environment contract.

options.title: Pause runtime adoption pending RFC direction
options.body: Hold the series until the RFC or maintainers settle the localization ownership and operator configuration model.

recommendation.title: Approve a documented process-locale contract
recommendation.body: Define precedence, supported surfaces, fallback behavior, and upgrade expectations for OPENCLAW_LOCALE before the series uses it broadly.

likelyOwner.reason: The author owns the proposed series design and can incorporate the chosen contract, though final product direction requires repository maintainer approval.
